status: First-pass narration verified against the scheduled scan, recorded Orka Bot conversation, Engineering task, and PR #36. The explicit demo bridge and usage gaps remain visible.

scenes.text: Orka is an execution and governance layer for AI agents. It runs specialized agents as teams, on infrastructure you control.
Here, a scheduled scan starts on its own. The reliability team examines a demo application for vulnerabilities in the source code.
Agents map the code, trace user input, and validate suspected issues against the source. Each retained finding includes evidence, so the next team has something concrete to act on.
A colleague opens Microsoft Teams and asks what needs attention. Orka explains the finding and its evidence in the same conversation.
A person chooses the fix. A small demo bridge passes the finding to Engineering, under that team's own permissions.
Engineering's coding agent prepares the patch and runs checks. Orka handles publication separately, so the coding agent does not need Git credentials.
The result is a real pull request, with a recorded delivery outcome and validation evidence. Reviewers can inspect exactly what changed.
Orka records task outcomes and available model usage, making the work measurable.
Teams is one example. Orka's gateway protocol lets adapters connect other channels, including Slack or Telegram.
Orka. Run agent teams. Stay in control.
